samf-junior-2025-r2-01.title: Halve at each split
samf-junior-2025-r2-01.body:
At each junction the balls split equally between the two pipes. To reach A a ball must go left at the top junction, left again at the next junction, and left again at the junction above A and B: three halvings. So $A$ receives $1000\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=125$ balls.

**Answer: 125**

samf-junior-2025-r2-02.title: Straight angle, then alternate angles
samf-junior-2025-r2-02.body:
The angles $3x$, $5x$ and $2x$ lie on a straight line, so $10x=180$ and $x=18^\circ$. The slanted segment crosses the two parallel lines, so $y$ and $3x$ are alternate angles: $y=3x=54^\circ$.

**Answer: 54**

samf-junior-2025-r2-03.title: Ratio parts
samf-junior-2025-r2-03.body:
The difference of $5-3=2$ parts is 12 sweets, so one part is 6 sweets. The packet has $8$ parts: $8\times6=48$ sweets.

**Answer: 48**

samf-junior-2025-r2-05.title: Slopes
samf-junior-2025-r2-05.body:
$BA$ goes 3 right and 3 up (slope 1) and $BC$ goes 3 left and 3 up (slope $-1$). The slopes multiply to $-1$, so the lines are perpendicular: $90^\circ$.

**Answer: 90**

samf-junior-2025-r2-05.title: Lengths
samf-junior-2025-r2-05.body:
$AB^2=18$, $BC^2=18$ and $AC^2=36$, so $AB^2+BC^2=AC^2$ and the angle at $B$ is a right angle.

**Answer: 90**

samf-junior-2025-r2-06.title: Overcount
samf-junior-2025-r2-06.body:
$35+42=77$ exceeds 65 by 12, and the boys who play both were counted twice. So 12 play both.

**Answer: 12**

samf-junior-2025-r2-07.title: Pass mark
samf-junior-2025-r2-07.body:
The pass mark is $15+3=18$, which is 40% of the total. $18\div0.4=45$.

**Answer: 45**

samf-junior-2025-r2-09.title: Maximise the boys
samf-junior-2025-r2-09.body:
There are 18 girls and 12 boys, and 20 pupils speak Sesotho. The fewest girls speak it when as many boys as possible do: all 12 boys, leaving $20-12=8$ girls.

**Answer: 8**

samf-junior-2025-r2-10.title: Extra wheels
samf-junior-2025-r2-10.body:
If all 14 cycles had 2 wheels there would be 28 wheels. The 10 extra wheels each belong to a tricycle (one extra wheel per tricycle), so there are 10 tricycles.

**Answer: 10**

samf-junior-2025-r2-11.title: Perimeter of an L
samf-junior-2025-r2-11.body:
The perimeter of the L-shape equals the perimeter of its bounding rectangle: width $11+17=28$ and height $x+15$ where $x$ is the height of A. $2(28+x+15)=106$ gives $x=10$. Rectangle A is $11\times10$, so its area is 110.

**Answer: 110**

samf-junior-2025-r2-12.title: Squares of primes
samf-junior-2025-r2-12.body:
A number has exactly 3 factors only if it is the square of a prime $p$ (factors $1,p,p^2$). The 2-digit squares of primes are $25$ and $49$. The largest is 49.

**Answer: 49**

samf-junior-2025-r2-13.title: Find the pattern in column C
samf-junior-2025-r2-13.body:
Column C holds $3,7,11,15,\dots$, i.e. $4n-1$ in row $n$, so row 100 has 399 in column C. In even-numbered rows the numbers run right to left, so column D holds one less than column C (e.g. row 2: C is 7 and D is 6). So row 100 has $399-1=398$ in column D.

**Answer: 398**

samf-junior-2025-r2-14.title: Distance is fixed
samf-junior-2025-r2-14.body:
Distance $=$ speed $\times$ time is the same for all three: $3\cdot20=60$. Then $4x=60$ gives $x=15$ and $5y=60$ gives $y=12$. $x+y=27$.

**Answer: 27**

samf-junior-2025-r2-15.title: Sums of ages
samf-junior-2025-r2-15.body:
All six sum to 180; the grandchildren sum to 48; so the grandparents sum to 132. With $g$ the grandfather: $g+(g-6)=132$, so $g=69$.

**Answer: 69**

samf-junior-2025-r2-16.title: Add lengths
samf-junior-2025-r2-16.body:
Let the square have side $x$. The top dimension 8 covers the left rectangle and the square; the bottom dimension 10 covers the square and the right rectangle. So the large rectangle has width $8+10-x$ and height $x$. Perimeter $=2(18-x)+2x=36$.

**Answer: 36**

samf-junior-2025-r2-17.title: Two orders
samf-junior-2025-r2-17.body:
The probability of shaded then non-shaded is $\frac25\cdot\frac35=\frac6{25}$, and the same for the other order. Total $\frac{12}{25}=48\%$.

**Answer: 48**

samf-junior-2025-r2-18.title: Triangular lattice
samf-junior-2025-r2-18.body:
Divide each side into 4 parts of $0.5$ cm and join to make a triangular lattice of small equilateral triangles of side $0.5$ cm. The lattice has $1+2+3+4+5=15$ points, each pair at least $0.5$ cm apart, so 15 points are possible.

**Answer: 15**

samf-junior-2025-r2-19.title: Equal speeds
samf-junior-2025-r2-19.body:
Let the train be $L$ metres long. Crossing a bridge means travelling bridge length plus $L$. $\frac{L+445}{21}=\frac{L+320}{16}$ gives $16L+7120=21L+6720$, so $5L=400$ and $L=80$.

**Answer: 80**

samf-junior-2025-r2-19.title: Extra time
samf-junior-2025-r2-19.body:
The extra $445-320=125$ m takes the extra $21-16=5$ s, so the speed is $25$ m/s. In 16 s the train travels $400$ m, which is $320+L$, so $L=80$.

**Answer: 80**

samf-junior-2025-r2-20.title: Girl is 4%
samf-junior-2025-r2-20.body:
The single girl will make up 4% of the people, so there must be 25 people in total: 24 boys and 1 girl. So $99-24=75$ boys leave.

**Answer: 75**

samf-junior-2025-r2-21.title: Volumes
samf-junior-2025-r2-21.body:
Water in A: $\pi\cdot8^2h=64\pi h$. Water in B: $\pi\cdot4^2h=16\pi h$. Capacity of A: $64\pi\cdot20=1280\pi$. So $80\pi h=1280\pi$ and $h=16$.

**Answer: 16**

samf-junior-2025-r2-22.title: Rhombus
samf-junior-2025-r2-22.body:
The shaded shape is a rhombus. Let its side be $x$ (the slanted side along the diagonal-corners) and consider the right triangle with legs 4 and $8-x$ and hypotenuse $x$: $x^2=16+(8-x)^2$, so $16x=80$ and $x=5$. The rhombus has base 5 and height 4: area $20\text{ cm}^2$.

**Answer: 20**

samf-junior-2025-r2-23.title: Express in the first two terms
samf-junior-2025-r2-23.body:
With first terms $x,y$ the sequence is $x,y,x+y,x+2y,2x+3y,3x+5y,5x+8y$. So $5x+8y=2025$, and $8y=2025-5x$. We need $2025-5x$ divisible by 8; since $2025\equiv1$ and $5x\equiv1\pmod8$ means $x\equiv5$, the smallest is $x=5$ (then $y=250$).

**Answer: 5**

samf-junior-2025-r2-24.title: Derangements
samf-junior-2025-r2-24.body:
Envelope $A$ can get $b$, $c$ or $d$. Say it gets $b$; then the arrangements of the rest with no matches are $B a,C d,D c$; $B c,C d,D a$; $B d,C a,D c$: 3 each time. Total $3\times3=9$.

**Answer: 9**

samf-junior-2025-r2-25.title: Relative speed
samf-junior-2025-r2-25.body:
Riding in opposite directions, they close at $x+2$ m/s and meet every time they cover one lap together: track length $=30(x+2)=30x+60$. We need $30x+60>200$, i.e. $x>4.67$, so the smallest integer is $5$.

**Answer: 5**
